The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed
Why, in plain words: Someone switched on a new monthly spending feature, and it sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that divides by zero, likely for shoppers who had not bought anything yet this month, so those pages failed to load.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 11m 10s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 40.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 8,025.67 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - refuted, put back when it did not help
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #548 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 03:30 UTC, not back to normal by 03:41:10 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 9 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:02:28 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 03:36:30 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 11, 2026, 03:41:10 UTC - PR #548, opened as a draft

Summary
The service broke at 03:30 UTC and was not back to normal by 03:41:10 UTC, at least 11 minutes 10 seconds later. 33.5% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 40.5% failed. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by at least 8,025.67 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Someone switched on a new monthly spending feature, and it sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that divides by zero, likely for shoppers who had not bought anything yet this month, so those pages failed to load. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help. On an earlier incident like this one, Argus had also reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature, and it was refuted there. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #548, for a person to review and merge. Account page requests could keep failing with a division by zero for as long as monthly-spend-feature stays on.

Impact
at least 11m 10s - since onset, still not back to normal
40.5% - peak error rate
4,830 - requests failed
1.0% to 33.5% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
at least 8,025.67 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, render_spend_summary calls average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases it made this month. The divisor is zero for any shopper who has bought before but not yet this month, so the account page request raises ZeroDivisionError. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service logged account page error rates far above their usual level.
  Evidence:
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 34 occurrences in 40 minutes, 03:00–03:39; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 03:35. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:37–03:39
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 20 occurrences in 10 minutes, 03:30–03:39. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:37–03:39
why 1 The account page requests failed because building the page raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The service logged this error during 03:30–03:39 UTC and not before.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 Requests reached that code because admin switched feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at 03:29:57 UTC. The service evaluated the flag as off during 03:00–03:28 UTC, partly on in 03:29 UTC, and on for every evaluation during 03:30–03:39 UTC. The division errors began in the first minute the flag was on for every evaluation.
  Evidence:
    P1 03:29:57 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 29 occurrences in 29 minutes, 03:00–03:28
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 192 / on 8 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 03:29
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 10 occurrences in 10 minutes, 03:30–03:39. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:37–03:39
    G5309
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 03:31; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change; the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 7 hours 30 minutes before Nov 11 03:40; the Investigator Agent read back 3 production changes.
      T7
      T8
      T25
      T26
    Shoppers closing their connections, the account page error logged before the onset: it was logged only during 03:00–03:29 UTC, while account pages were rendering normally.
      G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 39 occurrences in 30 minutes, 03:00–03:29
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 6 occurrences in 23 minutes, 03:06–03:28
why 3 Switching the flag on broke the page because, as Code-Fix read the source, the flag sends account pages through a monthly average per item whose divisor is zero for shoppers who have bought nothing yet this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
Contributing factors
- No test or check was seen that ran the code path monthly-spend-feature turns on against an account with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production. Code-Fix's reading says the existing tests do not cover that case. (AI-2)
- The flag went from a few evaluations on to every evaluation on in the next minute. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on rising errors were seen. (AI-3, AI-4)
- As Code-Fix read the source, a broad handler in serve_account_page turns any exception in the spend summary into a failed account page rather than leaving that section out. (AI-5)
- No on-call person was paged when the HighErrorRate alert fired on io-shop. (AI-6)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 03:29:57 UTC. Account page requests then began failing with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% to about 34%. No deployment was involved. | 0.93 | refuted
C2 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 03:29:57 UTC. This sent account page requests through src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, where line 47 raises ZeroDivisionError. The error rate stepped from about 1% to about 35% at 03:30 UTC. No code or configuration deployed, and latency, memory and CPU stayed flat. | 0.88 | refuted, as tested for C1

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 03:36:58 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | refuted, put back when it did not help
 | 03:41:10 | Proposed a fix: PR #548 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 03:30 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 03:36:05 UTC, 6 minutes 5 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #548 | open
AI-2 | Require that the code path a feature flag turns on in io-shop is covered by tests before that flag can be switched on in production. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Roll out io-shop feature flag changes to a small share of traffic first, then widen in stages. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Halt a staged flag rollout automatically, and switch the flag back, when the service's error rate rises above its baseline. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Make serve_account_page render the account page without the spend summary when the summary fails, instead of failing the whole page. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to page the on-call person. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Switch monthly-spend-feature off again in a way that reaches io-shop. Confirm at the service that its flag evaluation log lines read monthly-spend-feature=off and that ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py is no longer logged for account page requests. Keep it in place until the fault is fixed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-8 | Find out why io-shop kept logging monthly-spend-feature=on evaluations after the flag was switched off at 03:36:51 UTC: whether the change reached the service's flag evaluation at all, and if so through what cache or refresh. If it did reach the service, find out why account pages still failed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-9 | Before the Mitigation Agent judges a change it made, have it confirm from the service's own logs that the change reached the service. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 36 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at 03:30.
- 41 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 53 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 3 minutes 22 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action REFUTED - monthly-spend-feature was put back ON.
- 5 minutes 5 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #548.
What went wrong
- The Mitigation Agent judged the revert refuted while io-shop's own flag evaluations still logged monthly-spend-feature=on in 03:37–03:39 UTC, after the flag had been switched off.
- Argus found an earlier incident in memory, 9c1d4e7a-0000-4000-8000-00000000fee1, where reverting this same flag had been refuted, and tried the same revert again without first finding out why it had not helped then.
- The second investigation formed only C2, which blamed the same flag change that had already been tried, so it gave Argus nothing new to try.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py builds the list of purchases with in_current_month set, then divides account.total_this_month_cents by the length of that list. Its divisor is zero for any shopper who has bought before but not yet this month. That is a normal state for a real account, and it covers nearly every account early in a month. render_spend_summary calls this function whenever use_monthly_summary is set and use_typical_spend is not. So switching on monthly-spend-feature sent those shoppers' requests to a // with a zero divisor, and the broad handler in serve_account_page (src/io_shop/account_page.py) turned the ZeroDivisionError into a failed page.

The fix: when nothing was bought this month, the function now returns 0, which is the average spend per item over an empty month. Otherwise it divides exactly as before. The page then renders a figure for these shoppers whether the flag is on or off. Nothing is swallowed: the lifetime average (average_spend_per_item) is unchanged and still raises for an account with no purchases at all. The existing tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py and tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py assert that it raises and that the failure names a // line in spend_summary.py, and that path is untouched.

The tests: tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py gets two new cases using the existing an_account_with_no_purchases_this_month helper. One checks that the monthly average is 0. The other checks that render_spend_summary with use_monthly_summary=True returns 0. Against the current code both cases would raise ZeroDivisionError.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, some shoppers' account pages failed to load for {duration}. Someone switched on a new monthly spending feature, and it sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that divides by zero. The shoppers affected were likely those who had not bought anything yet this month. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, because no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus switched the monthly spending feature off, but that did not help, so Argus switched it back on. Argus has also proposed a fix. It is open as a draft and has not been put into effect.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
